fields.statement: QA cycle 2 with the branch built to a scratch path and run as a scratch root daemon (web token set): a real command-only plan run stopped at rhiza run gate on two open questions. The root merged inbox showed both with answer forms posting to /p/proj/actions/answer (csrf hidden field, statement HTML-escaped). A cookie+csrf POST answering the first got 200 'Answered. The run continues once its other questions are answered.' and wrote one Decision in the run's worktree; repeating it got 400 'Nothing to do' and wrote no second Decision; no csrf 403; blank text 400. Answering the last got 'Answered. The run continues.', the daemon resumed the run and its next step ran: the run succeeded and the inbox emptied. A second run with one question answered through rhiza question answer --run and the other through the web also resumed and succeeded; a web repeat of the CLI-answered one and an unknown question were refused. Answering an ended run 409, an unknown run 404, a missing question 400, no auth 401. Approve on a non-stopped or unknown run 'Nothing to do', empty run 'Nothing to approve'. Scoped go test ./internal/api -run 'TestWebAnswerAction|TestWebApproveAction|TestWebPauseAction|TestWebTokenSetting' and ./internal/web -run TestWeb pass.

QA cycle 2, scratch root daemon: cookie+csrf POSTs to /p/proj/actions/pause with scope project/daemon and paused true/false answered 'This project is paused.', 'The daemon is paused.', and the resumed forms, leaving rhiza.daemon.paused=false in rhiza.toml and rhiza.project.paused=false in the project's git config. Bearer POSTs to /retry, /abandon, /merge, /actions/retry, /actions/merge, /p/proj/actions/abandon, /p/proj/runs/X/retry were 404; /api/daemon.set, /p/proj/api/run.resume, question.answer and run.approve were 405.

QA cycle 2, scratch root daemon: page forms carry a csrf hidden field; a cookie POST to the answer action with no csrf and to the pause action with a wrong csrf got 403 and changed nothing; the page's csrf value acted; a bearer POST needed none.

QA cycle 2: rhiza daemon set rhiza.web.token replied 'set'; rhiza daemon settings showed 'set', and neither rhiza daemon status --json nor unauthenticated GET /api/daemon.settings, /api/daemon.status, /p/proj/api/daemon.settings, /p/proj/api/daemon.status contained the value. GET ?token= set the cookie (303). A wrong bearer and no auth got 401. With the token removed from rhiza.toml, POSTs got 403, pages showed no forms and GET / stayed 200.
